Q is a point on the zpf characteristic at 1.0 p.u. voltage. Across what does the vertical distance PQ in the figure give the voltage drop?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The plot has Voltage (p.u.) on the vertical axis and Field Current on the horizontal axis. Curve X is the upper open-circuit characteristic, and curve Y is the lower full-load zero power factor characteristic. A vertical line at the same field-current value passes from Q on curve Y at 1.0 p.u. voltage up to P on curve X, so PQ is the vertical voltage separation at fixed field current. Reasoning: At this same excitation, P represents the open-circuit generated voltage and Q represents the full-load zpf terminal voltage. The difference PQ is therefore interpreted as the internal voltage drop from generated emf to terminal voltage under the zpf load condition. In the standard synchronous-generator characteristic interpretation, this drop is across the synchronous reactance.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the vertical segment PQ is drawn at one fixed field-current value from the zpf curve Y at Q up to the open-circuit curve X at P. From the text, Q is the full-load zpf operating point at 1.0 p.u. voltage. Since P gives the corresponding open-circuit voltage for the same field current, the vertical separation is the internal voltage loss from generated emf to terminal voltage at full load. In the standard synchronous-generator characteristic interpretation, this vertical voltage drop is across the synchronous reactance. Answer: synchronous reactance.

method.method_draft: First read the image: PQ is a vertical voltage interval, not a horizontal field-current interval, between the upper OCC point P and the lower full-load zpf point Q at the same excitation. Then use the generator voltage equation under zpf loading: the terminal voltage at Q differs from the open-circuit generated emf at P mainly by the synchronous reactance drop I_aX_s. Because the zpf condition makes this drop appear along the voltage axis in the characteristic construction, the plotted distance PQ represents the voltage drop across synchronous reactance. Answer: synchronous reactance.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The figure plots Voltage (p.u.) on the vertical axis against Field Current on the horizontal axis. There are two rising curves: upper curve X and lower curve Y. A vertical line at a fixed field current intersects curve X at point P and curve Y at point Q. Point Q lies on the 1.0 p.u. voltage level, shown by a horizontal dashed line. Thus PQ is a vertical voltage interval at the same excitation, not a horizontal field-current interval.

Reasoning: Curve X is the open-circuit characteristic, so point P represents the open-circuit generated emf for that field current. Curve Y is the full-load zero power factor characteristic, so point Q represents the terminal voltage under full-load zpf operation for the same excitation. Under zpf loading in the synchronous generator characteristic construction, the difference between the open-circuit generated emf and the loaded terminal voltage appears as the armature-current drop across synchronous reactance, IaXs. Therefore the vertical distance PQ gives the voltage drop across synchronous reactance.
